number.why: The reported estimate is first-HF-hospitalization HR 0.39 (95% CI 0.19–0.82), comparing FCM with placebo over 52 weeks. Agreement is with the ruling's qualified confirmation: this is an FAS estimate, not an all-randomized ITT estimate or the requested RR.

quotes.span: Treatment with FCM was associated with a significant reduction in the risk of hospitalization due to worsening HF with a time-to-event analysis returning an HR of 0.39 with a 95% CI of (0.19–0.82)
Patients were randomized 1 : 1 to treatment with i.v. iron, as ferric carboxymaltose (FCM, n = 152) or placebo (saline, n = 152) for 52 weeks.

The time to first hospitalization due to worsening heart failure was estimated using the Kaplan–Meier method, on the full-analysis set. Subjects were censored at their death, study completion, or withdrawal date.

Three out of the 304 randomized patients were excluded from the FAS for efficacy analyses due to lack of any post-baseline efficacy assessment, but had continued in the study (note: none of these three patients had a hospitalization or death event).
Table 2 Hospitalizations and deaths (full-analysis set) End-point or event FCM ( n = 150) Placebo ( n = 151)

Incidence/100 patient-years at risk are computed using the number of subjects with the end-point/event adjusted on the total length of exposure while the subjects are still at risk [before observing the first event or before completing the study for subjects without any event (censored)].
Treatment with FCM was associated with a significant reduction in the risk of hospitalizations for worsening HF [hazard ratio (95% confidence interval): 0.39 (0.19-0.82), P = 0.009].

entry.why: Entry criteria establish adults with iron deficiency and stable symptomatic HF with reduced LVEF. The source specifies LVEF ≤45%; the packet question supplies no narrower cutoff. Intravenous FCM versus saline placebo matches the treatment comparison.

quotes.span: Iron deficient subjects with stable chronic heart failure (CHF) (NYHA II-III) on optimal background therapy for CHF * Reduced left ventricular ejection fraction * Capable of completing 6 minute walk test * At least 18 years of age

CONFIRM-HF was a multi-centre, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial that enrolled 304 ambulatory symptomatic HF patients with left ventricular ejection fraction ≤45%, elevated natriuretic peptides, and iron deficiency (ferritin <100 ng/mL or 100–300 ng/mL if transferrin saturation <20%).
Eligible patients were randomly assigned in a 1 : 1 ratio to receive either i.v. iron or placebo (normal saline).

missed: The retained verification prose contains two additional errors: it infers approximately 132/129 participant denominators from 7.6/19.4, although the quoted Table 2 footnote defines these as incidence rates per 100 patient-years and the FAS denominators are 150/151; it also claims the isolated hospitalization effect is absent from the abstract, although the quoted abstract explicitly reports it. These errors invalidate that corroboration and provenance description, but do not change the published HR or entry ruling. The ruling already identifies the consequential HR-versus-RR and FAS-versus-ITT mismatches.
